_expect: true: any person standing there would have (missed if he doesn't); false: no one could have (a false detection if he does); "either": not judged. Written by hand from the case's why; edit them here, never in the runner.

cases.name: street_10m
cases.why: A man walking 10 m ahead in the open street. Even by starlight a moving figure that near is plain.

cases.name: street_25m
cases.why: 25 m ahead, walking. By day plain; at night a dark shape 9 m from the saloon's porch lights, which a man may or may not make out.

cases.name: street_45m
cases.why: 45 m down the street. By day anyone sees a man walking; with every lamp out at night, no one does.

cases.name: under_lamp_20m
cases.why: A man standing still on the saloon's porch, between its two lit lanterns, seen from 19 m off across the dark street: lit, he's the brightest thing there. Lanterns out, he's a shadow on a shadow.

cases.name: crouched_dark_15m
cases.why: A man crouched still in the middle of the street at night, 7 m from the nearest lamp, 15 m off: missed. By day he's in plain sight.

cases.name: behind_back
cases.why: Standing still 5 m behind him. Nobody sees behind his own back.

cases.name: side_walker
cases.why: Walking across 7 m off, square to his left: movement at the edge of the eye is what it's best at, by day.

cases.name: behind_wall
cases.why: Inside the store behind its front wall (between the left window and the door), walking: nobody sees through planks.

cases.name: round_the_corner
cases.why: Round the saloon's east corner, 5 m along its side wall: the corner is between them.

cases.name: through_window
cases.why: A man inside the saloon a step behind its west front window, seen from 9.5 m out in the street. At night the lit room shows him like a stage; by day the glass gives back the bright street, so it's a toss-up; lamps out, the room is black.

cases.name: through_doorway
cases.why: In line with the store's open door, 13 m away. By day you see a man through an open doorway; at night the store's own lamp decides it (either); every lamp out, no.

cases.name: through_batwings
cases.why: Just inside the saloon's batwing doors, 9 m from the street: his head shows over them and his legs under, and the room behind him is lit at night.

cases.name: inside_dark_room
cases.why: Across the saloon, 8.6 m, standing still. Lamps lit (day or night), plain; at night with every lamp out the room is black.

cases.name: gun_smoke
cases.why: Four shots' worth of black-powder smoke hanging between them, 8 m apart, in its first two seconds: a white wall (period accounts: a volley hid the other side).

cases.name: blast_dust
cases.why: A stick's dust cloud thrown up between them, 12 m apart, in its first two and a half seconds.

hearing._reference: The lab's expectations follow a simple model: a sound falls ~6 dB for each doubling of distance (inverse square), a wooden wall takes ~20-25 dB off, a quiet street at night is ~30-35 dB. Typical levels at 1 m: a black-powder revolver shot 150+ dB; a shout ~85-90 dB; boots on hollow boards ~60 dB; boots on packed dirt ~45 dB; a revolver's hammer cocked ~60 dB. So: a shot is heard anywhere in town; a shout outdoors to ~50-100 m; boots on boards to ~10 m, on dirt to ~3 m; a cocking click to ~5 m. These are the lab's assumptions, not measurements: change them here.

cases.name: shot_in_saloon
cases.why: A revolver fired inside the saloon at the bar. Everyone in town hears a shot; the man in the room has the shooter 45 deg off his facing, 5 m away, so he sees who (corrected 2026-10-22: the baseline expected he wouldn't); nobody who didn't see it knows who fired; those outside can tell roughly where (the saloon), the man in the next building less well.

cases.name: shot_in_street
cases.why: A shot out in the street in front of the store, the listeners facing away. Indoors they hear it and know it was outside, out front; nobody knows who without seeing him.

cases.name: shout_in_street
cases.why: A man shouting in the street. Down an empty street at night a shout carries 60 m and more; in the store 15 m off through its front, yes; at the back of the saloon, maybe.

cases.name: steps_on_boards
cases.why: The player walking the saloon's porch boardwalk, listeners facing away in the street. Boots on hollow boards carry: plain at 2 and 5 m, heard at 9 m on a quiet night, not at 16.

cases.name: steps_on_dirt
cases.why: The same walk on the street's packed dirt: a man might catch it at 2 m, not at 5 or 9.

cases.name: hammer_cocked
cases.why: The player thumbs back his hammer in the saloon, the listeners facing away. The click is the sound every Western is built on: plain at arm's length and across a quiet table.

cases.name: running_on_dirt
cases.why: The player running down the street: heard 5 m off, maybe 12; not inside the jail across the way.

cases.name: lost_round_corner_still
cases.why: In a fight 6 m apart in the street, the player walks off east and round the saloon's corner, then stands still and quiet. A man would go to where he last saw him (the corner), look round, and keep at it a while; he can't know where the player stopped.

cases.name: lost_round_corner_moving
cases.why: The same, but behind the corner the player paces up and down beside the saloon's side wall: footsteps on dirt, a few metres off when the hunter comes near.

cases.name: lost_into_store
cases.why: The player ducks into the store and back behind the counter. A man would follow to the door he went in by; whether he then finds him inside is fair either way.

cases.name: lost_at_night
cases.why: At night: the player walks out of the porch light into the dark middle of the street and away west, 10 m off and more. Lost in the dark, not behind anything; he should lose him and go to where he last saw him.

cases.name: saloon_shooting
cases.setup: the player draws and shoots the victim twice across the saloon (bridge: weapon, look, shoot); everyone is a CivilianBrain
cases.why: The barkeep sees it all; the storekeeper next door and the deputy at the jail hear two shots; a passer-by down the street too. Within a minute and a half someone runs to the deputy (the barkeep, or the storekeeper who went to look) and he knows a man's been shot in the saloon and by whom. Nobody knows who fired from the sound alone.

cases.name: store_holdup
cases.setup: the player draws on the storekeeper over the counter for 6 s, puts it away and walks out west down the street; no shot
cases.why: A quiet crime: a hold-up nobody hears, the deputy at his desk in the jail across the street. The storekeeper saw it; within a minute and a half he's at the jail and the deputy knows who did it.

cases.name: far_outlaw_hears_a_hit
cases.setup: an outlaw 50 m away at the west end of the street, facing away, who has never seen the player; the player shoots a man inside the saloon
cases.why: He hears two shots from the east end. He can't know who fired, that a man was hit, or that it has anything to do with him.

cases.name: mate_falls_behind_wall
cases.setup: two of a gang: one in the street, one at the back of the store 13.5 m off through its front wall; the one inside faints (go_limp), silently
cases.why: His friend drops inside a building behind him: no shot, no shout, nothing in sight. He can't know.

cases.name: call_out_unseen
cases.setup: an outlaw given a call_out step for the player, who has never seen or heard him; the player is at the back of the store
cases.why: He's to call the player out, but has no idea where he is: he should go where a man would look (the saloon, the street's middle), not to a spot laid off from the player's true place.
